1.title: Get Set, Let's Go!
1.topic: getting ready for school in the morning (school, family, routine)
lines: *Get* up, | *get* up! | Get out of *bed*!
Get my *vest*. | My vest is *red*.
Get my *cup*. | Get my *egg*.
Get my *bag*. | Is it *big*? ↗
*Yes*! | Is *Mom* set? | Is *Dad* set? ↗
*Yes*! | We are *all* *set*. | *Let's* *go*! ↘
sounds: 입을 옆으로 살짝 벌리고 짧게 '에'. bed는 '벧'처럼 짧게 끝내요.
끝소리가 같아요. 앞소리만 바꿔 리듬 있게 읽어요.
질문은 끝을 올리고, Yes!는 힘차게 내려요.
1.expression: Start sleepy on “Get up,” ask the questions with a rising voice, and shout “Let's go!” as you run out the door.

2.title: The First Frost
2.topic: a boy discovers frost on a cold morning and watches it melt (seasons, weather, science)
lines: On a *cold* morning, | Leo *looked* | out the window.
The grass was *white* | and *sparkly*! ↘
Leo *asked*, | “Is it *snow*?” ↗
“It is *frost*,” | Mom *explained*. | “Tiny bits of *ice*.”
Leo *pulled* on his boots | and *rushed* outside.
He *touched* the icy car window | and *drew* a *heart*.
The sun *peeked* out. | The frost *melted* | drop by *drop*.
Leo *waved*. | “*Bye*, frost! | Come *back* tomorrow!” ↘
sounds: k, s 뒤 -ed는 짧은 t: looked '룩트'.
n, l 뒤 -ed는 d 소리: pulled '풀드'.
t, d 뒤만 '이드'로 한 박자 더: MEL-ted.
2.expression: Sound amazed at the sparkly grass, curious on “Is it snow?”, and wave goodbye cheerfully.

3.title: How to Make a Pinecone Bird Feeder
3.topic: making a pinecone bird feeder to help birds in winter (science, animals, seasons)
lines: When *winter* comes, | many birds have a *hard* time | finding *food*.
You can *help* them | with a simple *pinecone* bird feeder!
*First*, | ask a grown-up | to tie a *string* | around a big, *dry* pinecone.
*Next*, | *spread* sunflower seed butter | all over the pinecone.
*Then*, | *roll* it in a plate of *birdseed* | until it is *covered*.
*Finally*, | *hang* your feeder | on a *branch* | near a *window*.
Be *patient*. | It may take a few *days* | for the birds to *find* it.
Soon you might see *chickadees*, | *finches*, | or a red *cardinal*!
Keep a *notebook* | and write down | every bird you *spot*.
How many *different* birds | will visit *your* feeder? ↗
sounds: 입을 옆으로 당겨 길게 '이-'. spread의 ea는 짧은 '에'.
3.expression: Read it like a friendly craft teacher: clear and step by step, then end with a real question to your listener.

4.title: Peanut on the Loose!
4.topic: the class hamster escapes and the students follow a crumb trail to find him (school, animals, humor)
lines: On Monday morning, | Ms. Rivera *gasped*. | The hamster cage was wide *open*— | and Peanut was *gone*! ↘
“Nobody *panic*,” | she said, | but her voice sounded a little *squeaky*.
Everyone *searched* the classroom. | Dylan checked under the *bookshelf*, | and Sora looked inside every *backpack*.
Peanut was not in the *reading* corner. | He was not in the *lost-and-found* box, | either.
Then Sora *noticed* something strange: | a tiny trail of cracker *crumbs* | across the floor.
“*Detectives*,” | said Ms. Rivera, | “follow that *trail*!”
The class *tiptoed* silently | past the sink, | past the art cart, | all the way to her *desk*.
The trail *stopped* | at her bottom *drawer*, | which was open | just a *crack*.
Ms. Rivera *slowly* pulled it open, | and everyone *held* their breath.
There was Peanut, | curled up in a nest | of *shredded* paper, | *snoring* softly.
Next to him lay the *crumbs* | of Ms. Rivera's *granola bar*.
The whole class *burst* out laughing. ↘
Dylan *grinned*. | “Ms. Rivera, | I *think* | Peanut ate your *snack*!” ↘
That afternoon, | they put a brand-new *lock* | on Peanut's cage— | just in *case*. ↘
sounds: “Nobody panic,” (trying to stay calm), “Follow that trail!” (excited), “Peanut ate your snack!” (joking)
해설은 탐정 이야기처럼 긴장감 있게, 선생님은 침착한 척하지만 살짝 떨리게, 딜런은 장난스럽게 읽어요.
wide open— and Peanut was gone!
줄표(—) 앞에서 잠깐 멈췄다가 다음 말을 놀란 목소리로 말하면 이야기에 긴장감이 생겨요.
sh·c와 r 사이에 '으'를 넣지 마요. '슈레디드'가 아니라 shr을 한 번에 붙여 빠르게 이어요.
4.expression: Begin with a shocked gasp, build quiet suspense as the class tiptoes after the crumbs, whisper when the drawer opens, then let the laugh and Dylan's joke burst out.
practice: “Ms. Rivera, I think Peanut ate your snack!” (joking)
